summary: Comprehensive backend + frontend testing of SecureBank (Node/Express + Mongo + React). Wrote 29 pytest tests across auth, accounts, transactions (deposit/withdraw/transfer, fraud MEDIUM/HIGH flags, filters, analytics), beneficiaries, and admin RBAC — all 29 passing (100%). Frontend flows verified with Playwright: protected route redirect to /login, demo login lands on dashboard with Total Balance/Received/Transferred/Flagged stats, account creation on Accounts page adds a new card, Banking deposit succeeds, withdraw with excessive amount is blocked (400), large deposit shows MEDIUM/HIGH risk badge, transactions search + type-chip filters work, beneficiaries page loads, RBAC redirects normal user away from /admin, admin login lands on /admin console with Overview/Users/Accounts/Transactions/Suspicious tabs — all clickable and populated (screenshot shows HIGH/MEDIUM risk badges with reasons in ₹).

integration_issues.issue: API correctly returns 400 with 'Insufficient balance', but UI does not surface a visible '.error/[role=alert]' message locator — the user only sees a toast/message; consider adding a data-testid="banking-error" for testability

issues: React hydration warning: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' from Banking.js:111 (the emergent devtools wrapper injects a <span> inside <option>). Harmless in prod but noisy. Consider suppressing or restructuring the label.

action_items: (Optional) Add a data-testid on the banking form error/toast to make error states asserted programmatically.
(Optional) Silence the <span> in <option> hydration warning in Banking.js account dropdown.
critical_code_review_comments: Transfers in routes/transactions.js debit/credit two accounts across two independent .save() calls without a transaction/session — a failure between the two saves would corrupt balances. Wrap in a Mongo session/withTransaction for atomicity.
No rate limiting or brute-force lockout on /api/auth/login (playbook expects 5-attempt lockout).
JWT stored in localStorage (not httpOnly cookie) — acceptable per current implementation but noted per security playbook (httpOnly + CORS credentials pattern not used).

Fraud 'rapid transactions' counts ALL of a user's txns in last 60s regardless of type; the very first small deposit right after login also gets flagged MEDIUM once >=3 txns exist in the window (observed in Suspicious tab).
seed_data_creation: Created several TEST_ users via /api/auth/register during pytest; a few extra deposits/withdrawals/transfers on demo user's accounts; a throwaway suspended-then-reactivated user for admin RBAC test. No production data mutated.

context_for_next_testing_agent: All 29 pytest cases pass. loadscope splits classes across 2 xdist workers, so any test that mutates the shared demo user's global state must be avoided — the admin suspend/activate test therefore uses a throwaway user (do NOT change back to suspending demo). If you re-run the frontend deposit/withdraw flow immediately, expect fraud engine to tag small txns as MEDIUM due to the 3-in-60s rapid rule — this is expected behavior, not a bug.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — no functional defects blocking any feature.
